The site is Ceilidh & Session Tune Vault — Folk Music Archive & Tempo Notes, a community-forum web application for Traditional tune tune-sheet repository and tempo notes.

Owner brief: "Our weekly pub folk music session needs a shared digital tune repository and discussion board. Musicians should be able to look up traditional jigs and reels, view key signatures and ABC notation snippets, and post tempo notes or regional tune variations. Posted notes must be stored on the server so session players can review discussion threads after reloading the tune page."

Locale & copy conventions (en-GB): Use £ prices, British English spelling, day-month dates and .co.uk-style invented domains. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-20/reference.jpg).

Art direction: Ceilidh & Session Tune Vault — Folk Music Archive & Tempo Notes: the page for traditional tune tune-sheet repository and tempo notes, in a light palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #450a0a (fv-brown), #b45309 (fv-gold), #fefce8 (fv-parchment), #ffffff (fv-card), #fef08a (fv-border), #292524 (fv-text), #78716c (fv-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 8px, content-frame 1200px, control-border 1px solid var(--fv-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a posting control offered to a visitor who cannot use it; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of Ceilidh & Session Tune Vault — Folk Music Archive & Tempo Notes as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Musician name", "Tune title", "Dance rhythm", "Musical key", "Suggested tempo (BPM)", "Discussion note or variation").

User journey context: Browse the tune library and filter by dance rhythm such as reel, jig, or hornpipe. Inspect a tune's musical key, standard notation snippet, and historical background. Post a tempo suggestion or variation note, submit, and reload to confirm the note appears.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
